title: XRP News: ECB Settlement System Goes Live With XRPL-Linked Axiology
body: The European Central Bank has launched Pontes, its new infrastructure for settling tokenized securities in central bank money, with an XRPL-linked platform among the first four DLT operators connected to the system. The Eurosystem confirmed that Pontes went live on Sept. 21 with Axiology, Clearstream, Cashlink and SWIAT among its initial DLT operators. Banks including Deutsche Bank, Santander, Société Générale and the European Investment Bank have also completed onboarding. For XRP investors, however, there is an important distinction: the ECB is not using XRP or the public XRP Ledger. Axiology Uses XRPL Code, Not the Public Ledger Axiology operates a private, permissioned blockchain built using the open-source code of the XRP Ledger. The company explicitly says its infrastructure operates independently from both Ripple and the public XRPL. Only authorized financial institutions can operate nodes on the network. That makes the development significant for XRPL technology adoption, but it does not mean tokenized European securities are settling in XRP. Pontes instead connects participating DLT platforms with the Eurosystem's TARGET infrastructure so transactions can settle using central bank money. The distinction matters because XRPL's institutional footprint has already been expanding in other areas. Institutions have used the ledger for tokenized Treasury settlement involving Mastercard, Ondo and JPMorgan , while tokenized real-world assets have become an increasingly important part of the network's growth story. ECB Takes Tokenization One Step Further The ECB also announced that it is preparing to invest a small portion of its own funds in tokenized securities, with those transactions eventually settling through Pontes. Initial purchases are expected to focus on euro-denominated public-sector and supranational securities. That gives the launch a broader significance beyond Axiology. The ECB is moving from experiments toward live tokenized market infrastructure, while XRPL-derived technology has secured a place among the systems connecting to it. Coinpaper has already tracked how XRPL tokenization expanded into billions of dollars of real-world assets and how the network is being developed for institutional-grade lending and credit .

title: OpenAI's new math advisory group gets a say on releases but not on research pace
body: OpenAI has brought in nine preeminent mathematicians to advise on how it presents and releases its AI-generated math results. The company says the panel has no say in the pace of its research. Princeton’s Institute for Advanced Study hosts the unpaid panel The panel is called the Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence. It’s hosted at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, New Jersey, and lives online at agmai.org. Per OpenAI’s blog post , the group helps the company appraise the importance of new results and coordinate when and how they are released. It also weighs them against the field’s academic and professional norms, and advises on how to serve working mathematicians with the tools of OpenAI. It “will not be responsible for advising us on how to pace our internal progress on mathematics,” OpenAI wrote. OpenAI began training a new internal model on August 28. The company says the model has since solved over 100 long-standing open problems in most branches of mathematics, alongside a claimed solution to the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem . The initial members are François Charles of ENS-PSL, Camillo De Lellis of IAS and GSSI, Timothy Gowers of Collège de France and Cambridge, Martin Hairer of EPFL and Imperial College London, and Nikhil Srivastava of Berkeley and the Simons Institute. The list is rounded out by Oxford and INI’s Ulrike Tillmann, Stanford’s Ravi Vakil, IAS’s Edward Witten and Harvard’s Melanie Matchett Wood. Several of the members have Fields Medals of their own. OpenAI contacted some of them about an external advisory board, the group said in a guest post on mathematician Terence Tao’s blog, and instead they formed an independent group and invited others to join. Members take no payment from OpenAI, and they set their own membership. They can issue unsolicited recommendations. They can comment publicly on the impact of the company. The group said it would offer the same counsel to any AI lab whose models might reshape the field. Although we will give advice, we do not have decision making power at any AI company, and the responsibility for the decisions made by any company will rest with that company. The group said on its website . Its current job is to advise OpenAI on how to release the large batch of results produced by its internal model. The advisory group’s independence statement on agmai.org, captured September 22, 2026. 25 Fields Medalists warned AI labs on September 11 On September 11, 25 Fields Medal winners launched an open letter called “A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics.” AI labs racing to solve famed problems put mathematicians’ intellectual work at risk, it says. The declaration now lists 27 medalists and more than 7,800 endorsers. OpenAI cited the letter directly, framing the criticism as a reason to engage the community more thoughtfully. Three of the nine advisers are on the declaration. Martin Hairer signed it as a Fields Medalist, and Camillo De Lellis and Ravi Vakil endorsed it. The advisory group arrives weeks after OpenAI’s math claims turned contentious. As Cryptopolitan reported on September 8, OpenAI said an internal model showed finite-time blow-up for the forced Navier-Stokes equations, verified in the Lean proof-verification language. A few days earlier, related blow-up results were published by NYU mathematician Tristan Buckmaster and Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge. But Buckmaster said he was told “very little human input” went into OpenAI’s proof, an account he says fell apart on a call with the company. Buckmaster wrote that an entire team had worked the problem and that easier cases, Euler included, came first. He added that the prompt shown to him was itself generated by prompting Codex. Sébastien Bubeck, the OpenAI researcher who was at the center of the exchange, said the allegations were “false and inflammatory.” He denied using the mathematicians’ prompts or proofs. title: Circle Mint Launches BTC-Backed USDC Borrowing Through cirBTC on Arc and Ethereum
body: Circle on September 21 launched Digital Asset-Backed Borrowing for eligible Circle Mint LLC customers, allowing them to deposit Bitcoin, mint cirBTC and borrow USDC through integrated third-party lending markets on Arc or Ethereum without selling their BTC. The service places Circle Mint between a Bitcoin-backed collateral token and external DeFi lending venues, rather than making Circle the party that sets the loan terms. At launch, Morpho is the supported lending protocol. Circle said other markets, including Aave, are expected to be added. The rollout also coincided with cirBTC becoming available on Arc, extending a token that Circle had launched on Ethereum in June. Circle Mint routes BTC-backed borrowing through cirBTC Circle Mint customers deposit BTC, mint cirBTC and supply it from a customer-controlled wallet as collateral for USDC borrowed through an integrated lending market. Circle says the workflow is overcollateralized—the cirBTC supplied exceeds the value of the USDC borrowed—and that the USDC is delivered directly to the customer’s Circle Mint balance; repayment releases the collateral, according to its announcement . The minting step converts BTC into cirBTC before collateral is supplied, allowing customers to obtain USDC while retaining BTC exposure, subject to the selected lending market’s requirements. Circle frames the service as an expansion of Circle Mint rather than a standalone pool: borrowing occurs through an external protocol, while Circle provides the platform access and settlement path. Morpho sets the lending terms, with New York excluded Morpho is the first third-party lending protocol supported by the service, according to Circle. The company has also named Aave as an expected addition, without providing a timetable. Borrowing rates, collateral requirements and liquidation thresholds are determined by the lending market selected by the customer, not by Circle Mint, according to Cointelegraph’s reporting . Circle Mint handles the BTC-to-cirBTC path and the USDC balance destination. New York clients are excluded from the offering, Cointelegraph reported. The selected market’s rules determine the terms of an individual borrowing position, including the conditions for liquidation. Circle’s launch announcement describes availability for eligible Circle Mint LLC customers but does not give the full eligibility criteria. Further markets could give customers additional venues; Circle has said only that those integrations are expected. Official Circle image for Digital Asset-Backed Borrowing in Circle Mint. — Source: Circle Arc deployment follows cirBTC’s Ethereum launch cirBTC became available on Arc on September 21, the same date Circle introduced the borrowing feature. Arc said the token is backed 1:1 by BTC, with the underlying Bitcoin held by Circle National Trust and reserve data published through Chainlink Proof of Reserve . The Arc availability followed cirBTC’s earlier launch on Ethereum on June 8. That Ethereum release established the BTC-backed token before Circle extended it to Arc and connected it to the new borrowing workflow, according to Circle . For Circle Mint users, the Arc deployment means cirBTC can now serve as the stated collateral asset on either Arc or Ethereum in the company’s integrated setup. The launch begins with Morpho; the borrowing cost, collateralization standards and liquidation mechanics remain dependent on the market selected for the transaction. The new purchase was a small addition to the reported balance and left Strategy a large corporate holder of bitcoin. Cash, not ATM stock sales, funded the bitcoin purchase Strategy funded the latest bitcoin acquisition from its USD cash balance, rather than from proceeds of shares sold through its at-the-market, or ATM, offering. The Form 8-K said the company recorded no ATM sales during the purchase week. That disclosure separates the immediate source of funds for this transaction from an equity issuance program. It does not, by itself, establish how the cash balance had been built before the reporting period, but it makes clear that no ATM stock sales financed the disclosed 950-BTC buy during September 14 through September 20. The financing detail is especially relevant because Strategy’s bitcoin acquisition and preferred-share repurchase occurred in the same reporting window. Rather than reporting an ATM issuance alongside the bitcoin purchase, the company disclosed cash deployment across both activities. STRC repurchases exceeded the week’s bitcoin outlay During the period, Strategy’s filing showed two uses of capital: the company bought 950 BTC for $75.7 million and repurchased 1,771,238 STRC preferred shares for $174.0 million. The preferred-stock transaction was $98.3 million larger than the bitcoin purchase—more than twice the outlay. Strategy reported no ATM sales during the week; the filing identified cash as the funding source for the bitcoin acquisition. These disclosures capture the transactions completed in that reporting window and do not amount to a broader statement of Strategy’s future capital-allocation plans. The 846,000-BTC treasury was valued near $71.9 billion The Block reported that Strategy’s 846,000-BTC treasury was worth approximately $71.9 billion at the time of its publication. That is a market-value estimate, distinct from Strategy’s disclosed aggregate purchase cost of $63.80 billion. The company’s ledger places its average acquisition cost at $75,416 per bitcoin. The latest purchase, at $79,670 per bitcoin including fees and expenses, was made above that portfolio-wide average. Market value changes with bitcoin’s price, while Strategy’s aggregate purchase cost and average cost summarize what it paid to acquire the holdings. The latest disclosure therefore adds a fresh purchase and a funding detail to a treasury that Strategy reported at 846,000 BTC as of September 20. title: Aptos Launches Confidential APT on Mainnet, Encrypting Balances and Transfer Amounts
body: Aptos announced on Sept. 20 that Confidential APT is live on mainnet , giving users an opt-in way to encrypt APT balances and transfer amounts. Sender and recipient wallet addresses remain publicly visible, creating a privacy model that conceals values rather than the parties to a transaction. Confidential APT is live on Aptos mainnet Aptos announced that Confidential APT is live on mainnet, allowing users to opt in to encrypt APT balance amounts and transfer amounts. Participation is optional, and sender and recipient addresses remain visible in confidential transfers, according to Aptos' announcement. Zero-knowledge proofs validate hidden amounts Aptos said zero-knowledge proofs allow validators to verify transaction validity without seeing confidential transfer amounts. That allows the network to validate a transaction while the value remains undisclosed to validators. Encryption applies to balances and amounts, not wallet identifiers, Aptos said in a March post on its Confidential APT privacy features . AIP-143 moved from approval to deployment The mainnet announcement follows the execution of AIP-143, the governance proposal enabling APT confidentiality. Aptos governance records show the proposal was executed on April 24, 2026, at 19:35:59 UTC. The April governance action and September mainnet announcement mark separate stages: AIP-143 provided the approved protocol change, while the latest update confirms that Confidential APT is available on the live network. Visible addresses retain an accountability layer Keeping wallet identities visible may support accountability and compliance needs for businesses that want to avoid exposing transaction values. CryptoCompass reported that the launch is intended to support confidential payroll, treasury and business-to-business settlement, while preserving visible wallet identities for those purposes. For such transfers, the model leaves a public record of the counterparties while withholding the payment amount and relevant APT balance information. That mixed approach is now available to users who opt into Confidential APT on Aptos mainnet. Disclaimer: This article is provided for informational purposes only. title: Google Gemini Predicts Where XRP Will Trade On October 1, 2026
body: As artificial intelligence tools become increasingly integrated into financial analysis, investors and market observers are turning to large language models for short-term asset price projections. To test this trend, we asked Google Gemini a direct question: Where will XRP trade on October 1, 2026? The result was a detailed, multi-factor analysis covering technical chart structure, institutional capital flows, protocol developments, and the current regulatory environment. Before diving into the specifics, Gemini XRP in the $1.60 to $1.72 range by October 1, highlighting that as the headline target. The Forecast and its Basis At the time of the query, XRP was trading at approximately $1.49, showing bullish momentum after the recent crash following the CLARITY Act cloture vote . Gemini described its projection as “a single, unified bullish projection,” implying a roughly 7% to 15% move from that baseline. The model identified four primary drivers behind this target: a scheduled protocol upgrade, regulatory developments, institutional inflows, and technical chart structure. Protocol Upgrade as a Near-Term Catalyst The most time-sensitive factor is the XRPL Batch V1.1 hard activation, scheduled to trigger automatically on September 29. The upgrade enables bundling of up to eight transactions into a single fee, reducing costs for institutional payment networks. Gemini noted that such developments “typically act as positive price catalysts in the days immediately preceding and following activation,” making the October 1 window particularly relevant. Regulatory Clarity Through Administrative Action On the legislative front, the Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act failed Senate cloture vote at 49-50 . Gemini argued this carries limited impact, pointing instead to CFTC and SEC administrative rulemaking as establishing “clear commodity treatment and secondary-market exemptions” for XRP. The court ruling protecting XRP’s non-security status remains intact and continues to underpin institutional confidence. Mid-September Stripe integrations enabling AI-driven micro-transactions on the XRPL add a layer of “non-speculative, daily transactional demand,” according to Gemini. Technically, Gemini identifies $1.60 to $1.68 as the primary overhead liquidity target, with secondary resistance near $1.80. XRP recently reclaimed its 200-day exponential moving average and flipped the $1.40-$1.45 range into structural support following a 7.8% breakout. The Bear Case Gemini’s forecast carries one defined invalidation point. If XRP loses its $1.39-$1.42 support zone before October 1, the bullish scenario would be delayed, likely returning the asset to the lower end of the range observed in late August. title: This Signal Has Flipped to Altcoin Season as Crypto Rally Spreads Beyond Bitcoin
body: Glassnode’s Altcoin Cycle Signal flipped from Bitcoin season to altcoin season this week, the on-chain analytics firm has reported. This is after an August rally that had mostly bypassed altcoins gave way to broader participation across the market. Signal Says the Market Has Widened The Glassnode signal compares Bitcoin’s performance against a market-cap-weighted basket of the top 250 altcoins, minus stablecoins. High readings often mean altcoins are outperforming, while low readings mean BTC is leading. Additionally, the chart shows Bitcoin’s price line changing color according to the prevailing regime, with orange representing Bitcoin season and blue representing altcoin season. The primary cryptocurrency rallied through mid-August while the signal stayed orange, then it turned blue today as BTC’s price flew past $87,000. “The first rally in August saw altcoins stay relatively flat while BTC moved,” Glassnode wrote. “However, today’s rally has ignited the full breadth of the altcoin market.” In another post, the analytics platform noted that Bitcoin was trading above both the True Market Mean and the short-term holder cost basis, levels that have historically defined a sustained uptrend when price holds above them. The Elliott wave count also has BTC nearing the target for a fifth wave, with the daily RSI diverging from price, a setup analyst Darkfost says could be foreshadowing a pullback toward $74,500 before the asset goes up any higher. Bitcoin itself was changing hands above $85,000 at the time of writing, up 5% in 24 hours and more than 10% across the week, after breaching $87,000 on Monday, the first time it had hit that level since the end of January. ETH also boasted a 10% climb of its own in one week that has taken it past $2,700. Elsewhere, BNB crossed $800 for the first time since late January, XRP jumped from around $1.40 to above $1.50, and Dogecoin led the larger-cap alts with a 24-hour gain above 15%. All that winning pushed the total market cap 3.6% to over $3 trillion per CoinGecko, with Bitcoin’s share sitting at 57%. A Rally Built on a Rough Week As CryptoPotato reported, last week brought several macro headwinds, including the Senate voting against advancing the CLARITY Act and the Federal Reserve raising interest rates for the first time since July 2023, pushing BTC down to a multi-week low near $75,000 before it reclaimed its 50-week moving average and climbed back above $80,000. You can watch the video below for more on how the market reacted when the Fed raised interest rates. Meanwhile, ETH’s move past $2,700 has split opinion, with analyst DANNY not convinced. They called the setup a trap and expect a slide toward $1,500 before any real breakout.
